title: From Copilot to Colleague: Trustworthy Agents for High-Stakes - Joel Hron, CTO Thomson Reuters
talk_summary: Thomson Reuters' CTO describes shifting from 'helpful' assistants to 'productive' agents in high-stakes legal/tax domains, framing agency as tunable dials (autonomy, context, memory, coordination). Key transferable lessons: decompose legacy systems into tools agents call, build the whole system before optimizing, and treat human eval variance as a first-class problem.

takeaways.technique: Decompose legacy systems into agent-callable tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than rebuilding from scratch, they expose existing domain engines (tax calculation engine, validation engine, litigation search/fetch/citation-compare) as tools the agent invokes, so deterministic domain logic stays authoritative.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what agents have allowed us to do is to really decompose these legacy applications and decompose the components of them as tools that agents can now use

takeaways.technique: Human eval variance as a measured baseline
takeaways.what_they_do: They quantify that even expert human raters swing >10% on identical question sets a week apart, and use that noise floor to interpret whether system changes are real improvements; they combine coarse preference signals with finer rubrics for hill-climbing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I could give the same set of data like question response to the same people a week later and we see 10 plus percent swings in accuracy
takeaways.numbers: 10+ percent swings in accuracy by the same raters on the same questions a week later

takeaways.technique: Build the whole system before optimizing components
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue against over-indexing on 'minimal' in MVP: only after building the full end-to-end system could they see which components actually needed work versus which were absorbed by the agentic system itself.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it wasn't until we actually like built the whole system that we could see the whole system operate and we could understand you know what components of that system do we go need to go spend time on

takeaways.technique: Agency as tunable dials per task risk
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat autonomy, context, memory, and coordination as separate levers set by task risk tolerance, rather than a binary agentic/not-agentic choice.
takeaways.evidence_quote: these are dials that can be used to uh to to sort of tune what the experience and how much agency the experience has

takeaways.technique: Agent writes intermediate notes, rationalized at end
takeaways.what_they_do: During deep research the agent writes notes to itself about findings along the trajectory, then synthesizes those notes into a final report with hard citations to source records.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the model will write notes to itself about what it is learning, what it's finding. And at the end of the flow, we'll sort of rationalize those notes together
